contentHtml:
Real estate does not operate in isolation. Every transaction REALTORS® facilitate is shaped by policies, regulations and laws that influence property rights, housing development, taxation, financing and consumer protections. For REALTORS® serving Williamson and Bastrop counties, understanding the role of policy and advocacy is essential to protecting your business and the communities you serve.

Advocacy ensures the voice of the real estate industry is present when decisions impact housing and property ownership.

Why Policy Matters to REALTORS®

Government decisions influence nearly every aspect of the housing market. Zoning ordinances, permitting timelines, development regulations, infrastructure planning, property taxes and lending policies all shape the environment in which REALTORS® work.

Local decisions about development approvals or infrastructure expansion directly impact housing supply and affordability. State legislation influences property tax structures, consumer protections and licensing standards. Federal policies often affect lending regulations, housing finance programs and fair housing enforcement.

Without strong advocacy, these decisions could be made without the perspective of professionals who work directly with buyers, sellers and communities.

REALTORS® provide a unique perspective. You see firsthand how housing policies affect families purchasing their first home, sellers navigating the market and communities experiencing growth.

Through organizations like the Five Points Board of REALTORS®, Texas REALTORS® and the National Association of REALTORS®, our profession maintains a unified voice advocating for policies that protect property rights, promote housing opportunity and support a healthy real estate market.

One of the most important tools supporting this advocacy is TREPAC — the Texas REALTORS® Political Action Committee.

Investing in Advocacy Through TREPAC

TREPAC is the primary vehicle through which REALTORS® support candidates who understand the importance of property rights, housing access and a strong real estate market. Contributions to TREPAC help ensure lawmakers hear directly from the real estate industry when policies affecting housing are considered.

Investing in TREPAC is not about political parties — it is about protecting the ability of Texans to buy, sell and own property. TREPAC supports leaders who prioritize responsible housing policy, economic growth and the long-term stability of the real estate market.

For REALTORS® in Williamson and Bastrop counties, supporting TREPAC helps ensure the interests of property owners, homebuyers and the real estate profession are represented at the local, state and national levels.

Protecting Property Rights

Advocacy plays a vital role in protecting private property rights, which remain a cornerstone of homeownership and economic stability. Policies affecting land use, taxation, infrastructure development and housing regulations can have long-term consequences for property owners and communities.

By sharing insight with policymakers and participating in advocacy initiatives, REALTORS® contribute to balanced solutions that encourage growth while protecting property ownership.

Advocacy at the Local Level

As Williamson and Bastrop counties continue to grow, local government decisions increasingly shape housing supply, development patterns and infrastructure planning. REALTORS® play an important role in these discussions by providing insight into market conditions, housing demand and consumer needs.

At Five Points Board of REALTORS®, we remain committed to supporting our members through advocacy, education and engagement opportunities. By staying informed, participating in advocacy efforts and investing in initiatives like TREPAC, REALTORS® help ensure the future of real estate in our region remains strong, resilient and opportunity-driven.

When REALTORS® stay engaged in policy and advocacy, we protect more than an industry — we protect the fundamental right of property ownership.

The Women’s Council of REALTORS® Austin recently hosted one of its most highly anticipated events of the year — the annual Purse Bingo fundraiser — and it was a tremendous success! The sold-out event brought together real estate professionals, community members and local supporters for an evening full of excitement, networking and giving back.

From the moment doors opened, the energy in the room reflected the camaraderie and generosity that have come to define Women’s Council gatherings. Guests enjoyed multiple rounds of bingo while competing for stunning designer purses and prizes throughout the night. The mix of friendly competition, lively conversation and shared purpose made the evening one to remember for everyone

More importantly, the event also served a meaningful purpose by supporting Hope Alliance, the evening’s featured charity. Attendees helped raise awareness and support for the organization’s mission of assisting individuals and families impacted by domestic violence and sexual assault. Hope Alliance has long served as a vital resource in Central Texas, providing emergency shelter, counseling and advocacy for survivors who turn to the organization in their most difficult moments. Partnering with a charity of this caliber underscored the Women’s Council’s commitment to using its platform to drive real impact beyond the real estate industry.

WCR Austin continues its mission of empowering and elevating professionals within the real estate industry through education, leadership development and strong community connections. From continuing education classes and expert panels to networking opportunities and community outreach events, the organization remains focused on helping industry professionals grow both personally and professionally. Members regularly point to the value of the relationships they build through the council — connections that translate into referrals, mentorships and lifelong friendships across the Austin real estate community.

The Austin chapter has built a reputation for programming that blends substance with experience. Whether members are gathering for a charitable evening like Purse Bingo, attending a market update from a respected economist or sharpening their professional skills in a designation course, the council consistently delivers events worth showing up for. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear from Carl Pikus with IPX 1031 Exchange as he presents an informative class covering all things related to 1031 exchanges. This educational event is designed to provide valuable insights for real estate professionals looking to better serve their clients and expand their industry knowledge.

For those unfamiliar, a 1031 exchange is a tax-deferral strategy that allows investors to sell one investment property and reinvest the proceeds into another like-kind property without immediately paying capital gains taxes. Understanding the timelines, identification rules and qualifying properties involved in a 1031 exchange can be the difference between a smooth transaction and a costly misstep for clients. Pikus’s session will give REALTORS the working knowledge they need to recognize when an exchange may benefit a client
and to confidently coordinate with a
qualified intermediary.

The program is especially timely given current market conditions in Texas, where investor activity continues to play a meaningful role in both residential and small commercial transactions. Agents who understand 1031 exchanges position themselves as more valuable advisors and often unlock repeat business from investor clients who appreciate working with someone fluent in the strategy.

head: Advocacy in Action — 2026 Wins Deliver Historic Fed Housing Reform; Local Gains for Central Texas
excerpt: REALTORS® wear many hats — trusted advisors, neighborhood experts and advocates for our communities. contentHtml:
REALTORS® wear many hats — trusted advisors, neighborhood experts and advocates for our communities. Expanding access to homeownership has long been at the heart of what we do, and for ABoR, that work now spans 100 years in Central Texas. This year, our advocacy reached new heights, culminating in a landmark federal housing bill and local wins already shaping the region.

Federal Advocacy — REALTOR® Impact in Washington, D.C.

In June, ABoR members joined thousands of REALTORS® at NAR’s 2026 Legislative Meetings to advocate for key legislation, including:

More Homes on the Market Act: Incentivizes long-term homeowners to sell, increasing inventory.

21st Century ROAD to Housing Act: Reduces regulatory barriers and modernizes federal housing programs.

Revitalizing Downtowns and Main Streets Act: Encourages residential use of underutilized commercial spaces.

Association Health Plans Act: Provides REALTORS® access to affordable health insurance.

Those meetings paid off. One week after ABoR members were on Capitol Hill, Congress passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act — the most significant federal housing legislation in nearly 20 years, combining nearly 50 reforms to increase supply and make homeownership more attainable nationwide. This win reflects REALTORS® who showed up, spoke up and invested through TREPAC.

Local Advocacy — ABoR in Action Across Central Texas

REALTOR® Advocacy happens every day — not just at the Capitol, but in city halls and county courts across Central Texas. So far in 2026, ABoR has secured several local wins with the Austin City Council:

HOME Improvements: Council initiated amendments removing regulatory bottlenecks limiting the HOME Initiative’s reach, expanding smaller, more attainable housing options in Austin’s most desirable neighborhoods.

Missing Middle and Mixed-Use Zoning Reform: Council initiated new zoning districts allowing townhomes, cottage courts and small-scale multi-unit buildings across Austin.

Comprehensive Efficiency Assessment Program: Council unanimously established a citywide framework for ongoing, independent review of city departments — a win for taxpayer accountability.

New Rental Fee Disclosure Requirements: Council adopted disclosure requirements for landlords with five or more units, with ABoR ensuring the threshold protects agents and property managers from
unintentional capture.

Data-Driven Advocacy — Putting Unlock MLS Research to Work

Beyond legislative wins, ABoR is transforming how advocacy gets done. Better data leads to better policy, and by leveraging Unlock MLS data for original research, we’re equipping policymakers and members with the evidence needed to advance housing reforms.

Our “HOME Impact Report,” released this spring, is a prime example. Using Unlock MLS data, the report confirmed the HOME Initiative is producing smaller, more efficient homes at significantly lower price points than traditional new construction — evidence that gave the Austin City Council confidence to pass the HOME Improvements Resolution.

Moving Forward Together

Our 2026 progress is real, but so is the work that remains. Housing affordability isn’t solved once; it takes sustained advocacy at every level of government. As we celebrate 100 years of ABoR, our mission remains the same: fight for smart housing policies and help more Central Texans achieve the American Dream. None of this is possible without engaged members willing to show up, speak up and invest.

As your association President, I encourage you to get involved. There is strength in numbers. To get started, email advocacy@abor.com or visit UnlockMLS.com/Advocacy. Together, we can shape policies that protect homeownership for the next century.

As we look toward the months ahead, we are proud of the members who represented Austin so well in Washington, D.C., and we are energized by what lies ahead with our 2027 Board Elections. June is recognized nationally as Homeownership Month, a time to reflect on homeownership and its role in building strong communities. For REALTORS® serving Williamson and Bastrop counties, this month also highlights the connection between real estate professionals, civic leadership and lasting community impact.

Homeownership is more than a financial milestone. It represents stability, opportunity and investment in a community’s future. Every time a REALTOR® helps a buyer purchase a home, that transaction contributes to neighborhood stability, local economic growth and stronger civic engagement.

Research consistently shows homeownership has a powerful impact on communities. Homeowners are more likely to invest in their neighborhoods, support local businesses, participate in schools and civic organizations and contribute to their cities’ vitality.

In Williamson and Bastrop counties, where population growth continues to shape new developments, REALTORS® play an essential role in helping families plant roots. From first-time buyers to families relocating to Central Texas, REALTORS® guide individuals through one of life’s most meaningful decisions, contributing to the creation of stable neighborhoods and thriving communities.

REALTORS®’ impact extends well beyond individual transactions. They often serve as community leaders, advocating for responsible development, supporting housing initiatives and participating in local civic organizations. REALTORS® work alongside city leaders, economic development organizations, builders and community groups to support responsible growth. These relationships help ensure that as our counties expand, development remains thoughtful, sustainable and aligned with community needs.

Many REALTORS® also volunteer through charitable initiatives, local boards and nonprofit organizations, demonstrating that they are not only business professionals but also dedicated community partners invested in the long-term success of the places we live and work.

Homeownership Month also lets us reflect on expanding housing opportunities for future generations. As demand grows throughout Central Texas, maintaining access to homeownership remains an important priority for the region’s continued success.

REALTORS® help support housing opportunity by educating consumers, advocating for policies that protect property rights and working collaboratively with industry partners to encourage responsible housing development. Organizations like the Five Points Board of REALTORS® also play a key role by providing education, resources and advocacy that strengthen the profession while supporting healthy housing markets.

At the center of all of this is the REALTOR® — a trusted professional who helps individuals navigate the homebuying and selling process. Every showing, open house and closing represents a family building a future, a neighborhood growing stronger and a community becoming more connected.

As we celebrate Homeownership Month, the Five Points Board of REALTORS® proudly recognizes the impact our members have across Williamson and Bastrop counties. Through professionalism, civic leadership and a genuine commitment to service, REALTORS® continue to strengthen communities and help make the dream of homeownership possible for families throughout Central Texas.

The future of real estate is being shaped by more than inventory, interest rates and market cycles. It is also being shaped by the future of work — how people live, where they work, what they expect from their homes, and how those shifts influence housing decisions.

For REALTORS® in Williamson and Bastrop counties, these changes are already happening in real time. Remote work, hybrid schedules, flexible lifestyles and changing family needs have all influenced what consumers are looking for in a home and community. Buyers are often considering not just location and price, but how a property supports work, daily life, convenience and long-term goals. For many households, proximity to quality schools, walkable amenities and reliable broadband now weighs as heavily as square footage or a short commute.

As our region continues to grow, REALTORS® are helping clients make decisions in a market that looks very different than it did just a few years ago. That makes local expertise more valuable than ever.

Why Advocacy Matters

As the future of work changes the way people live and buy, advocacy becomes even more important. Issues like housing supply, infrastructure, transportation, land use, property rights and affordability are all connected to the future of our communities. Those decisions directly affect the markets REALTORS® work in every day. Local advocacy means showing up for water capacity, road expansion and utility planning long before a subdivision ever breaks ground.

Advocacy helps ensure that the voice of the REALTOR® is part of those conversations. REALTORS® understand how policy affects buyers, sellers, homeowners and housing opportunity in real time. We see what happens when affordability becomes strained, when growth moves faster than infrastructure, or when decisions create unintended barriers to homeownership.

For that reason, advocacy is not separate from real estate. It is part of protecting the future of the profession and the people we serve. A strong advocacy presence supports thoughtful growth, responsible development, and policies that keep communities strong and sustainable.

The REALTOR® of the Future

The future of work in real estate will require more than contract knowledge and pricing skills. It will require REALTORS® who are adaptable, tech-savvy, locally informed and able to guide clients through decisions shaped by changing lifestyles and expectations.

Today’s REALTOR® must be prepared to communicate value clearly, build trust quickly, and understand how technology and market shifts are changing the client experience. Consumers still need trusted professionals who can provide context, strategy and confidence in a complex environment.

That is why local leadership matters, especially as competition for buyers and listings grows more sophisticated. REALTORS® who stay informed and engaged will be better positioned to lead in the future.

The Role of Five Points Board of REALTORS®

At Five Points Board of REALTORS®, we believe the future of real estate belongs to professionals who stay connected to their local board, their local market and their advocacy efforts. Through education, resources, professional development and advocacy, we help REALTORS® in Williamson and Bastrop counties stay prepared for what comes next.

As our communities continue to evolve, REALTORS® will continue to play an important role in shaping not just transactions, but the future of housing, growth and community in Central Texas. Through advocacy, professionalism and leadership, our members help ensure that the future of real estate remains strong, informed and locally grounded.

In today’s real estate environment, data is one of the profession’s most valuable assets. From property details and market statistics to client records and transaction information, REALTORS® rely on accurate, timely and secure data every day. As technology continues to shape the future of real estate, securing that data has become just as important as understanding contracts, pricing and market conditions.

For REALTORS® in Williamson and Bastrop Counties, this issue is especially important because real estate is increasingly driven by digital tools, online platforms and shared information systems. The more connected the industry becomes, the more responsibility professionals have to protect the information entrusted to them. At Five Points Board of REALTORS®, we believe data security and advocacy go hand in hand because protecting the integrity of real estate information is essential to protecting the future of the profession.

Why Real Estate Data Matters

Real estate data supports nearly every part of the business. It helps REALTORS® advise clients, analyze market conditions, price homes accurately, market listings effectively and guide consumers through informed decisions. MLS data, public records, transaction history and client communications all play a role in helping REALTORS® provide professional, trusted service.

When that data is compromised, misused or accessed improperly, the impact can be significant. Security threats, data breaches, inaccurate information and misuse of listing data can affect not only business operations but also client trust. In an industry built on credibility and professionalism, trust is everything. Protecting real estate data is not just a technical issue; it is a professional responsibility.

Data Security Is Part of Professionalism

As REALTORS® use more digital platforms, cloud tools, mobile apps and artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems, strong data practices become even more important. Simple habits such as using secure passwords, verifying sources, protecting login credentials, monitoring system access and being cautious with client information can make a major difference.

But data security is bigger than individual best practices. It also depends on policies, standards and industry advocacy that help protect how information is collected, shared and used. REALTORS® need systems that are secure, ethical and built with the interests of property owners, consumers and professionals in mind.

Why Advocacy Matters

This is where advocacy becomes critical. Advocacy in real estate is not only about taxes, pr55555555looperty rights and development. It is also about protecting the systems and standards that keep the profession strong. Securing real estate data means supporting policies and industry efforts that defend the accuracy, ownership and responsible use of listing information and client-related data.

As technology continues to evolve, REALTORS® need a voice in conversations around data access, cybersecurity, platform standards, AI and how real estate information is managed. Without advocacy, decisions about real estate data could be shaped by outside forces that do not fully understand the needs of the profession or the communities we serve.

The REALTOR® Role in the Future

For REALTORS® in Williamson and Bastrop Counties, the future of real estate will depend on both strong data practices and strong advocacy. Consumers expect professionals who can use modern tools wisely while also protecting their privacy and trust. REALTORS® who stay informed, follow secure practices and support advocacy efforts will be better prepared for the future.

At Five Points Board of REALTORS®, we are proud to support members through education, resources and advocacy that strengthen the profession. Protecting real estate data is part of protecting our clients, our business and the integrity of the market. As the industry continues to evolve, REALTORS® must remain both informed and engaged because securing data and securing the future of real estate go hand in hand.
